title: Contractor Year-End Marketing Checklist for 2027
meta: A blunt, do-it-this-week checklist to clean up your Google profile, stack reviews, fix your site, and stop missing calls before 2027.
short: Four concrete year-end fixes that cost little and print money in spring.
statLabel: fixes you can finish before New Year's

body.answer: The year-end tune-up is four jobs: claim and clean your Google Business Profile, ask recent customers for reviews, fix your website's phone and CTA, and set up missed-call text-back.
body.html:
Winter is slow. Good. That's when you fix the stuff that's been leaking money all year. You don't need a new logo or a $5k website. You need four boring jobs done right.

Here they are in order. Claim and clean your Google Business Profile. Ask your recent customers for reviews. Fix the phone number and the call button on your site. Set up missed-call text-back so you stop losing leads to voicemail. That's the whole list. Do it this week and spring prints.

body.h2: Claim and clean your Google Business Profile
body.answer: Claim the profile, fix the name, phone, hours, and service area, and add real photos. It's free and it's the single biggest local lead source.
body.html:
Your Google Business Profile is the first thing a homeowner sees when they search your trade plus your town. If it's unclaimed, wrong, or empty, you're handing jobs to the next guy. Claim it. Then make the name, address, phone, and hours match your site exactly.

Add real photos of your trucks, your crew, and finished work. Pick the right categories. Fill in the service area. Walk the whole thing top to bottom using our Google Business Profile checklist for contractors so you don't miss a field.

body.h2: Ask your recent customers for reviews
body.answer: Most homeowners read reviews before they call, and most won't seriously consider a shop under 4 stars. Ask every happy customer from this year, now.
body.html:
Most homeowners read online reviews before choosing a contractor, and most won't seriously consider a shop under 4 stars (BrightLocal Local Consumer Review Survey). That's the game. Reviews decide who gets the call before you ever pick up the phone.

You've done dozens of jobs this year. Text the happy ones a direct link to leave a review. Keep it short: 'Thanks again — would you mind leaving us a quick Google review? Here's the link.' Our guide on how to get more Google reviews gives you the exact asks that work, and the reviews hub covers the rest.

body.h2: Fix the phone, the CTA, and missed-call text-back
body.answer: Put a tap-to-call number above the fold, make the main button obvious, and turn on missed-call text-back so no lead dies in voicemail.
body.html:
Open your site on your phone. Can you see a phone number and a call button without scrolling? If not, fix that first. On a phone, the number should be tap-to-call. The main button should say 'Call' or 'Get a Quote,' not 'Learn More.'

Then set up missed-call text-back. When you can't grab the phone, an automatic text goes out so the lead doesn't call the next guy. Speed matters: responding in 5 minutes instead of 30 makes you up to 100x more likely to connect with a lead (Lead Response Management study, Prof. James Oldroyd). More on that in speed to lead for contractors. If you'd rather a human set this up with you, talk to Aaron.

faq.q: How long does the year-end checklist take?
faq.a: A focused afternoon for the profile and site fixes, plus a week of texting recent customers for reviews. None of it needs a developer.

faq.q: Do I need to pay for any of this?
faq.a: No. Claiming your Google profile, asking for reviews, and fixing your own site buttons are all free. Missed-call text-back is cheap and pays for itself fast.
The Google Business Profile. It's the biggest free lead source for local contractors and most shops have theirs half-filled or wrong.
